correctness.rationale: A dependence forces one point into the affine span of the others, precluding the corresponding leave-one-out trace; an all-positive trace bounds the size by k+1. On an independent support use zero/one prescriptions on independent differences from a positive anchor and extend the positive span inside the kernel to dimension k. The empty trace comes from a parallel coset of a k-flat containing the support, valid since k<d. Counting ordered independent tuples and dividing by m! gives the coefficients. For a direct online upper bound, in the all-positive branch of any shattered tree every query must extend the current affine span: otherwise the next negative edge could not be realized. A witness to the all-positive leaf is a k-flat, allowing at most k+1 independent positives, or at most k+1−t beyond the fixed set T. Extending T inside a shattered independent support gives the conditional lower bound on the original domain. This also handles k=0 and t=k+1. The supplied finite trace checks were inspected, not rerun. Rows marked ldim_exact False are not exact adaptive-rank checks.

evidence: The former proves the VC/Littlestone equality for nontrivial linear-combination zero sets over any field using the all-positive path independence obstruction; the latter §VI states Ldim=d+1 for its real affine-subspace family. broader_coverage.reasoning: The numerical overlap alone is not used to infer coverage for all k. The inspected proof of Proposition 3.6 gives the mechanism: a dependence on earlier positive vectors rules out the opposing branch. Here the all-positive vectors are bounded by the rank of the witnessing flat, so the same argument works unchanged at exact rank and after adjoining T.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: After placing an independent support in a (k+1)-flat, passing from its hyperplanes to ambient exact k-flats is immediate. Counting its supports is counting independent sets. Starting the same all-positive argument with the span of t previously fixed independent points charges t dimensions to the rank budget, and completing these points to a shattered support gives equality. No separate conditional combinatorial classification is needed.

evidence: Affine homogenization x ↦ (1,x) makes affine independence ordinary independence in the affine chart. Guingona et al. equivalent_formulations.reasoning: For the target support, do the prior hyperplane construction on the affine chart of a (k+1)-flat containing it. All nonempty traces are realized by proper affine hyperplanes there, hence by exact k-flats in V; the empty trace is realized by a parallel translate of its containing k-flat. Dependency rules out every other support by the same linear closure obstruction. This is an exact reduction, not an identification with all projective flats on their full point domain.

value.rationale: This is a useful teaching example, but as a research finding the polynomial repackages classical independent-support counts and the exact-rank and conditional equalities require only the already understood trace construction and span budget. There is no harder transcript law, new enumeration, or nonroutine exact-rank obstruction left over. Renaming the same counts and combining these direct consequences does not supply a substantive mathematical gain.
